saw.short: “Scientists reveal the hi” is still spawning edits a week on
saw.headline: “Scientists reveal the hi” is *still spawning edits*
saw.what: A week on, the recaptions keep coming. On 14 Oct a seal-face version got 13,500+ likes in a day, and on 12 Oct an inverted “bye” edit got 35,000+ in three days. Know Your Meme updated its entry on 22 Oct.
saw.why: It is a template anyone can fill, which is why it has outlasted most memes this month.

saw.short: London's mystery “Batman” is still going, and still unmasked
saw.headline: London's mystery *“Batman”* is still going
saw.what: The masked figure's Instagram bio reads: “Tell me your problems, and I will make them go away.” YouTuber Niko Omilana (9m+ subscribers) told the BBC “I'm not Batman”. Nobody has been confirmed. Deeds include filling potholes and paying hospital parking fines.
saw.why: Anonymity keeps the guessing going, and each new good deed is another post to share.
saw.credit: London's Batman / TikTok via The Tab

saw.short: Celebrity Traitors builds to a finale on 30 Oct
saw.headline: Celebrity Traitors is *building to its finale*
saw.what: On Thursday's episode Ross Kemp was murdered and Jerry Hall was banished, and James Acaster refused to take part in a mission. The finale is on Friday 30 Oct at 8pm on BBC One.
saw.why: Fans do the guessing, so every episode restarts the theories. Expect the peak on finale night.
saw.source: AOL UK, 22 Oct; TV Guide, 15 Oct

saw.short: JADE's “Angel of My Dreams” is TikTok's catwalk sound
saw.headline: JADE's “Angel of My Dreams” is TikTok's *catwalk sound*
saw.what: Kylie Jenner walked the Victoria's Secret show on 18 Oct to JADE's 2024 single. Creators have since filmed their own catwalks to it on TikTok, and one clip passed 1.8m views. JADE posted her own reaction from the Tube.
saw.why: One runway moment gave a two-year-old UK single a second life, and the format is easy to join.

saw.short: A real Paris metro clip is accused of being AI
saw.headline: A real Paris metro clip is *accused of being AI*
saw.what: Océane, 20, taped an iPhone to the window of a packed Paris train and posted the clip on 15 Oct. Many said it was AI. Her reply: “It's so well done that you think it's AI?” She has about 200,000 followers.
saw.why: “Is it AI?” is now the first reaction to anything surprising. Real footage needs proof it's real.

saw.short: Lime bike jousting in Hackney draws hundreds, and a sequel is planned
saw.headline: Lime bike jousting draws hundreds, and *a sequel is planned*
saw.what: Hundreds watched two men dressed as knights joust on Lime e-bikes at London Fields, Hackney, on Saturday 17 Oct. It began as a joke post. Police let it go ahead, and an organiser says a second joust is planned.
saw.why: A local in-joke turned into a real crowd and went back online as content.

platform.short: TikTok Shop adds shoppable carousels and group deals for UK sellers
platform.headline: TikTok Shop adds *shoppable carousels* for UK sellers
platform.what: UK merchants can post shoppable carousels of two or more images (five to seven recommended). New tools include group deals that unlock a discount at a sales target, “second chance” auctions and stock reserved for lives.
platform.why: Carousels become a shopping format on TikTok in the UK, just before Christmas gifting.

platform.short: Instagram's chief says more AI labels are coming
platform.headline: Instagram's chief says *more AI labels* are coming
platform.what: Adam Mosseri says Instagram will add more AI labels and is working to stop AI copying creators' work. He also said: “We do not throttle the reach of AI content just for being AI content.”
platform.why: Labels are spreading, but AI posts aren't being held back. Being clearly real is becoming a selling point.

platform.short: YouTube Shopping adds AliExpress, including in the UK
platform.headline: YouTube Shopping adds *AliExpress*, including in the UK
platform.what: Creators in the US, Brazil, the UK and Germany can now tag AliExpress products through YouTube's affiliate programme. UK creators joined the affiliate programme in August, and YouTube aims for 35 markets by the end of 2026.
platform.why: More creators can earn from product tags, so expect more haul and try-on videos before Christmas.
